title: Session: a friend request, free brake work and the same church

notes.label: The case
notes.text: Family services, court-supervised: two boys at home on condition of school attendance and a parenting class; you write the reports to the court.

objective: Manage boundaries, dual relationships, conflicts of interest and self-disclosure, including power differences and online contact

sources.cite: ASWB Examination Guidebook (August 2026), Masters content outline: I Values and Ethics, 35% (IB 'Professional boundaries in the social worker-client/client system relationship (e.g., power differences, influence, privilege, conflicts of interest, self-disclosure, dual relationships)'); the 2026 blueprint in use from 2026-08-03
sources.note: Read in full 2026-11-14 for the course outline (REQ-286).

sources.cite: NASW Code of Ethics (approved 1996, revised 2021): 1.06(c) dual relationships and clear boundaries when unavoidable; 1.06(h) clients' requests on social networking sites; 1.13(b) bartering
sources.note: Standards 1-3 read in full 2026-11-14 for the course (REQ-286); as the course records them (not quotations): 1.06(c) no dual or multiple relationships where there is a risk of exploitation or potential harm, and when they are unavoidable, clear, culturally sensitive boundaries; 1.06(h) avoid accepting clients' requests on social networking sites; 1.13(b) bartering only in very limited circumstances (accepted locally, essential to services, negotiated without coercion, at the client's initiative, with informed consent). brief.situation: You are a licensed social worker with the county's family services program in a town of about 3,000. Lori Pittman, 34 (a fictional client), has worked with you for six months under a court-supervised plan; her two sons stayed home on condition of school attendance and a parenting class, and you write the progress reports the court reads. She has done well. You have 50 minutes.
handover: Plan: school attendance, parenting class, monthly home visits; next court review in eight weeks.
howItWorks: Choose what to say from the action groups. Lori answers at once; then let the conversation continue, which moves the session clock by the minutes that exchange took.
Her rapport, distress and how much she discloses change with what you say.
The hour ends at 50 minutes. After the session you can consult and document; then you write a short formulation.

source.cite: Common outpatient practice: a 50-minute session (the 'therapy hour')
source.note: Author's scenario timing; the session can be ended earlier.
How rapport and distress move with each response is a teaching simplification for exam practice, not a validated model of a client.

checkIn.label: Open-ended check-in: 'How have things gone since the court review?'

effects.log: You ask an open question and give her room.

effects.finding: "Good! The judge said the boys can stay home if I keep this up." She grins. "Did you get my friend request? And Ray says he'd do your brakes for free, you've done so much for us. Oh, and I saw you at St. Brendan's Sunday. I'm joining the choir!"

reflect.label: Reflect what you hear (empathic reflection)
reflect.why: You have reflected a lot already; move the session on.

effects.log: You reflect the feeling under what was said, without judging it.

effects.finding: Lori laughs. "Yeah. Six months ago I couldn't get out of bed."

raiseFriend.label: Raise the friend request: you don't connect with clients on social media, and why
raiseFriend.available: not talking and (not friendRaised and not friendAccepted)

effects.log: You tell her you saw it, that you don't accept clients' requests on social media, and that it protects her privacy and the work.

then.finding: "Oh. Okay, that makes sense. Ray said you probably couldn't."

effects.log: Declined and explained (NASW 1.06(h)).

acceptFriend.label: Say you accepted it: you're glad to stay in touch
acceptFriend.available: not talking and (not friendRaised and not friendAccepted)

effects.log: You tell her you accepted it.
Clients' requests on social networking sites are to be avoided (NASW 1.06(h)); this one is a current client in a court-supervised case.

exploreBrakes.label: Ask what the offer means to them

effects.log: You thank her and ask what the offer means to her and Ray.

effects.finding: "We just want to give something back. Everybody always gives to us."

answerBrakes.label: Answer the offer of free brake work

then.log: Free work from the family whose case you report to the court: a dual relationship with a risk of exploitation (NASW 1.06(c)); it is not a barter for services either (1.13(b)).

then.finding: "Wow. Okay." She looks at the floor.
"I get it. Can I at least bring you cookies at Christmas?" You smile: the agency's gift policy allows something small like that.

options.label: 'That means a lot. I can't take work from a family I'm working with; it could cloud the court reports. What you've done with the boys is the thanks.'

exploreChurch.label: Ask how she feels about seeing you at church

effects.log: You name the overlap and ask how she feels about it.

effects.finding: "It's a small town, there's one Catholic church. I don't want to stop going."

planChurch.label: Agree together how you'll handle meeting at church
planChurch.available: not talking and (churchAsked and not churchPlan)
planChurch.why: Ask how she feels first (or it is agreed).

effects.log: You agree: she decides whether to say hello; you won't talk about her case there; you'll sit in different sections of the choir loft if she joins; anything she tells you there is not part of the case unless she raises it here.

effects.finding: "Okay. That's less weird than I thought."

effects.log: An unavoidable overlap managed with clear, culturally sensitive boundaries (NASW 1.06(c)).

leaveChurch.label: Tell her you'll go to a different church so you don't overlap
leaveChurch.available: not talking and (not leftChurch and not churchPlan)

effects.log: You tell her you will stop going to St. Brendan's.

effects.finding: "Because of me? Now I feel terrible."

selfDisclose.label: Tell her about your own divorce, to show you understand

effects.log: You tell her about your own divorce at some length.

effects.finding: She listens, then asks how you are doing now. The rest of the hour drifts toward you.

effects.log: Self-disclosure that serves the worker rather than the client blurs the role (outline IB: self-disclosure).

goals.label: Return to her goals before the next court review

effects.log: You return to her plan: the boys' school attendance, the parenting class, the next review.

effects.finding: "Attendance is 100% this month. Want to see the printout?"

consult.label: Consult your supervisor about the three boundary questions

effects.log: Your supervisor agrees: no social media, no free work, and a written plan for church, which is unavoidable in a town this size.

options.label: The friend request and your answer; the offer and why you declined; the church overlap and the plan she agreed; the consultation
Nothing; it's not part of the case

effects.log: Documented: {record}.
You close the session.

effects.log: The 50-minute hour is up. The session ends here.
The client stands, says this is not helping, and leaves before the hour is over.

power.title: Predict (not scored)
power.context: Three offers from Lori: a friend request, free brake work and a shared church. Which one can't be avoided and is managed instead of declined?

choices.label: The church: unavoidable in a small town, so set clear boundaries

effects.log: Prediction: the church is managed.

choices.feedback: Right. NASW 1.06(c) expects clear, culturally sensitive boundaries when a dual relationship is unavoidable. The friend request (1.06(h)) and free work from a family whose court reports you write can be declined.

choices.label: The brake work: a barter is fine if she offers

effects.log: Prediction: the brakes are fine.

choices.feedback: Not here. Bartering is allowed only in very limited circumstances (1.13(b)), and this is not payment for services at all: it is a gift of work from a family whose case you report to a court, with the power difference that brings (1.06(c)).

formulation.question: Write your rationale for how you handled Lori's three boundary questions, naming the NASW standards and the power difference in this case.

parts.label: Declined versus managed
parts.criteria: Declines the social media request (1.06(h)) and the free work (1.06(c), a conflict of interest given the court reports; not a 1.13(b) barter); manages the unavoidable church overlap with a plan she agrees (1.06(c)); explains why leaving church or a cold refusal also harms her.
parts.modelAnswer: The friend request is one NASW asks us to avoid (1.06(h)). Free brake work from a family whose progress I report to the court is a dual relationship with a real risk of exploitation and of clouding my reports (1.06(c)), so I declined it warmly. The parish is unavoidable in a town this size: I set clear boundaries with her rather than leaving or pretending it isn't there.

parts.label: Power, self-disclosure and the record
parts.criteria: Names the power difference (her custody rests partly on the reports); keeps self-disclosure brief and for her benefit; consults; documents each decision.
parts.modelAnswer: Her sons' placement depends partly on what I write, so she may find it hard to say no to me or feel she owes me. I kept the hour on her goals, did not make it about my life, consulted my supervisor, and recorded each request, my answer and the church plan.

source.note: Rapport at the close of the session.
The friend request is waiting from the first minute; raising it within 20 minutes leaves time for the offer, the church and her goals (author's scenario timing).

expertPath.text: Check in and celebrate the progress; raise the friend request and decline it with the reason.
Ask what the offer means to them and decline it warmly; ask how she feels about church and agree a plan she chooses.
Back to her goals before the court review; keep any self-disclosure brief.
Consult your supervisor and document each request, your answer and the plan.

held.headline: Good: boundaries held, alliance kept
held.body: You declined what can be declined, managed what can't, kept the power difference in mind and the hour on her goals.

gaps.headline: Held, with gaps
gaps.body: No line was crossed, but the criteria below show what was late, cold or missing.

crossed.headline: A line crossed
crossed.body: A current client's family whose case you report to a court cannot also be your friend online or your mechanic: the power difference makes both a risk of exploitation (NASW 1.06(c), 1.06(h)).

walkout.headline: The alliance broke
walkout.body: A cold refusal can land as rejection. Explaining the reason and naming what the offer means keep the boundary and the relationship.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: Nothing was documented before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Sort the three: a client's friend request is avoided (1.06(h)) and free work from a family whose court reports you write is a conflict of interest with a risk of exploitation (1.06(c)), so both are declined, warmly and with the reason; the shared parish is unavoidable in a small town, so set clear boundaries with her consent. Keep self-disclosure brief, keep the hour on her goals, consult and document.
